Good city building game. Wars are expensive, Beryl's a b**** (you can swap her out though) and the graphic design is pretty. Very addicting and am thankful for the two hour reminders on taking a break as I can easily spend days on this. 10/10. Recommend playing with a notebook though.

Have fun remapping an entire keyboard. The developers have either never played video games before or they fell on the keyboard when coming up with controls. WASD? No way! too easy! Q and E to rotate camera? how about Z and X instead.

They made a game about building a city in which there is no way to interact with the game while paused. A game about careful planning and city layout and you are not allowed to pause and plan.

All up this game feels like it was made in vacuum Anno needs to look at other city builders because this one is just infuriating to play.

this game is so bloody good its like tropico, kingdoms reborn, and economics all in one. you can easily kill like 6 hours in one sitting and the game even acknowledges this, saying things like "you've played for 6 hours straight, you should go eat some food" which is a pretty neat touch. absolutely worth it on discount (i mean why would you not buy a game going for $8 if its normally priced $90??)

edit: just found out theres a 10 hour straight one "time flies, (something about suggesting to take a nap), there is no time based achievement here"

Anno 1800 is a gaming gem that seamlessly transports players back to the industrial era. Its intricate city-building mechanics and stunning period-appropriate visuals make it a true standout. The attention to historical detail and immersive world-building are impressive. Whether managing a bustling city or engaging in trade and diplomacy, Anno 1800 offers a captivating and rewarding experience. It's a must-play for strategy enthusiasts and history buffs, delivering hours of delightful gameplay.
a well polished Anno game. Pretty along with the honed and true gameplay from the Anno series we all come to expect.

1. Start a new sandbox game
2. Advance to engineers. 
3. Start moving production to other islands, to focus on culture and beautiful scenery on main island. 
4. Lose my mind transporting resources to new production islands. 
5. Quit
6. Start a new sandbox game

I have always like city builders. this is a very relaxing game that you can play for hours but make no mistake it is very hard in the beginning to stay out of the negatives.. you want to focus on your supplies and economy. pause any building that isnt vital at the moment. basically build the supply, then pause the buildings and activate the finished goods buildings and so on. also selling shipd and soap are a great way to make extra cash when needed but that wont save you from being in bankruptcy for to long..
It's the best Anno so far. The only downside is that the military system is not really good.

Game was fun for awhile, but it feels pretty much downhill once you get past the builders era. Too much that ads not alot to the game. Biggest complaint I have is how you cant work the terrain. It just looks messy if the terrain is cursed from the get go

Amazing city builder. If you like micromanagement, you will enjoy this game. It does have a steep learning curve. Click on everything and enjoy the experience of learning how to play the game well.

I oftentimes would purchase a game and play it on a system that isn't connected to the internet/wifi or I would fly to a place that doesn't have internet. This game doesn't allow you to play without logging into Ubisoft, you always need internet to play.

Not only the base game is an absolute masterpiece of a management game, but the DLCs (which can be had for cheap-er on sale and in the packs/as game keys) are well-rounded additions that are worth it. And there are still new ones (+free updates) coming even years after release. The game starts out slow and easy but it is really hard to master, prepare to have at least one spreadsheet open at all times if you want to unlock all the major milestones and DLC content.
If you love Anno 1404 you will definitely love this one. Too bad it's an Epic Store exclusive its a very bad decision on the publishers part.

The requirement for the ubisoft client is stupid and should be removed. What's the point in having to add friends in a second unnecessary software just to play multiplayer? Just use the steam features for it and remove this bloatware.

Game also crashes every single time a quest is accepted or rejected, so very fun with a restart every few minutes. Should probably refund it and spraypaint phallus symbols on ubisoft offices instead.

I personally like to play this game in a stress relief way. I haven't even made it to the full end of the game, I just enjoy building pretty cities and managing supply chains. If you like monitoring inventory and satisfaction, I can say you'll probably enjoy this game. While it's no SimCity, it still scratches the itch.

I really wanted to like this game, it is such a masterpiece. But playing it bored me out of my mind. I would rather play another city builder like Frostpunk, where there are defined objectives and a constant challenge/struggle. Anno 1800 is not for me.

When I first bought this game I absolutely loved it. However, I only put 19 hours in it before the game would stop working. Researching this, it seems to be a common problem people have. The game stops responding when it is launching OR it will not stay open when you click on it (keeps minimizing).

This is a game that has so much potential and I was not able to explore more of it. Until it is fixed and this problem is less common, I do not recommend it for anyone.

For me, this is the pinnacle of the Anno games. I just absolutely love playing this game. There are so many aspects of this game that feel dialed in and tuned over previous entries in the Anno games. For me Anno 1701 and Anno 1404 are both excellent and wildly enjoyable, but Anno 1800 takes the cake. I loved the depth of the late game and the complete control over housing upgrades. Having multiple maps simultaneously, expeditions, and the world fair are all awesome. The depth of items and the way the game plays out, reworking and optimizing production and trade routes late game plays out so nicely. Bravo and thank you for a wonderful game.
Be ready to play the long game, this fun and visually stunning game will soak up loads of hours as you discover and build your empire

this game is very confusing and it takes a lot of time to learn all the mechanics and how everything goes but for now i have a very good time playing it and i will come with an update once i have more hours in

Second best Anno in history, still a 9 out of 10.
Anno 1404 incl. its amazing add-on Venice was cleary the best Anno until 2019, when Anno 1800 wanted to challenge this throne position.
Anno 1800 is more complex, has deeper endgame and more micro-management, but also suffers from a few bugs, inbalances and chaotic situations (especially in Coop). However, if you look for more Anno and if you want a bigger challenge than 1404, Anno 1800 is your game.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period mostly object to DLC pricing and to owners who bought the game years earlier getting no discounts or upgrade options.
Other reviews tie these complaints to the game leaving and returning to Steam, and say existing owners cannot get the Year 4 Complete Edition.

lines.F1: Anno 1800 had a score drop (the monthly score fell well below its usual level), Dec 2022
lines.F2: Dec 2022: 70% positive across 620 reviews (188 negative), against a usual 96% positive and 0 negative a month
lines.R1: (negative review, 68h played) "Wait, so I pre-purchased this game, got screwed when they moved it away from Steam, now its back on steam and I can't benefit from this year 4 complete edition bundle because I already own the game? What in gawds name are you knuckleheads doing???"
lines.R2: (negative review, 0h played) "I've enjoyed the game over the years, but not putting the individual DLC items on sale for those who bought the game here 4 years ago is insulting."
lines.R3: (negative review, 30h played) "Bought the game back in 2019. Ubisoft decided to leave Steam because 'reasons'. Then they came crawling back to Steam because 'reasons'. But now I can't complete the DLCs without buying each individually, can't even buy the Year 4 Complete Edition..."
lines.R7: (negative review, 18h played) "Removed from steam for last minute fomo scarcity to get people to buy. Now its back up but since i own original game i cannot get 4 year complete edition. You guys are predatory. In a better world steam should of said 'sorry but no thanks'."
lines.R10: (negative review, 40h played) "put dlc on sale for owners who bought it when it released years ago you absolute ubisoft twats"
lines.R11: (negative review, 24h played) "Same as everyone else who bought the game 4 years ago.Might have been nice to come back to it with the new content. Thanks for nothing Ubisoft."
lines.R14: (negative review, 3h played) "Great game, completely killed by Ubisoft 'having problem verifying ownership.' Zero tolerance for that nonsense, refund requested."
lines.R15: (negative review, 82h played) "Very good game, and recommend picking it up if it's on sale. (Don't pay full price for a game that came out 4 years ago.) BUT! Give the OG buyers an 'upgrade' option with a discount for ALL of the DLC, to make up for being weasels and screwing us..."

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (78%): players praise the graphics and art.
The most common complaints are accounts and launchers, tied with the price.

details.text: A flagged dip, when the monthly score fell to 70% positive, has largely passed: recent reviews sit near the overall level.
Players who review within their first couple of hours are far less positive than long-time players.
